attack_paths.narrative: GET /fetch?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/<role> is fetched server-side (app.py:35). Terraform allows IMDSv1 (infra/main.tf:25), so no session token is required and the role's temporary credentials are returned to the attacker. No authentication protects the route (MAN-001). Not validated at runtime; static chain only.
attack_paths.title: Anonymous SSRF to AWS credential theft

executive_summary: This sample application is not fit for deployment. Unauthenticated users can execute code on the server (unsafe deserialization, command injection), read the database (SQL injection), and pivot from an SSRF flaw to cloud credentials because the instance allows IMDSv1. The CI workflow lets anyone who opens a pull request run code with repository secrets. Fix the five immediate items first, rotate every credential found in the repository, then address the infrastructure exposure.

findings.remediation: Do not check out or run PR head code in pull_request_target; use pull_request, or split into an unprivileged build + privileged workflow_run.
findings.title: pull_request_target checks out untrusted PR code

findings.remediation: Never unpickle untrusted data; use JSON or a schema-validated format. Sign data with HMAC if pickle is unavoidable.
findings.title: Unsafe Python deserialization (pickle and friends)
findings.triage_reason: request.data passed straight to pickle.loads on an unauthenticated POST route: pre-auth RCE by construction.

findings.description: Hardcoded cloud credentials can be harvested from source, history, packages and build artifacts.
findings.evidence: Value AKIA…[redacted 20 chars] (entropy 4.12). Secret redacted; it was not used or validated.

findings.description: All ten Flask routes and all Express routes are reachable without a session or token; there is no auth middleware, decorator or gateway configuration in the repository.
findings.evidence: app.py defines @app.route handlers with no login_required/before_request hook; server.js mounts handlers directly on `app` with no auth middleware; no gateway/ingress auth config present.
findings.impact: Every other weakness is reachable by anonymous internet users, raising each to its pre-auth severity.
findings.remediation: Introduce a default-deny authentication layer (before_request hook / Express middleware mounted before routes), then per-route authorization checks; add a test that enumerates routes and asserts 401 without credentials.
findings.title: No authentication or authorization on any HTTP route

posture.statement: Critical risk: at least one confirmed critical issue or critical attack path.

posture_statement: Critical. Multiple independent pre-authentication code-execution paths were confirmed by static tracing, and no authentication layer exists on any HTTP route. Runtime testing was not performed.
trust_boundary_hints: Client -> server API boundary: every route/resolver needs authn + object/function-level authz review.
Application -> datastore boundary: verify parameterization and least-privilege DB credentials.
Server -> external network boundary: check SSRF controls, TLS verification, timeouts, and unsafe consumption of third-party responses.
Application -> OS boundary: verify no untrusted input reaches shell/exec arguments.
Application -> filesystem boundary: path traversal, upload validation, storage outside webroot.
Untrusted data -> object graph boundary: deserialization of attacker-controlled bytes.
Contributor -> CI -> cloud/registry boundary: workflow triggers, token permissions, secret exposure.
